1. Murrin et al. (2024) A systematic analysis of the contribution of genetics to multimorbidity and comparisons with primary care data. medRxiv. https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.05.13.24307009

2. Additional columns:
neg_log_10_p_value: -log10 p-value
rs_id: variant rsID
p_value: p-value
q_statistic: heterogeneity test statistic
i2: heterogeneity test statistic
n_studies: number of studies included (published consortia meta-analyses count as 1 here)
n_samples: number of samples included
effects: heterogeneity summary, where each study is coded as '+' for increased effect of the effect_allele, '-' for decreased effect of the effect_allele, '0' for no effect of the effect_allele, at a pre-specified significance threshold, and '?' if the study did not report an effect for the variant.

3. Additional information
Genetic associations results from the GEMINI multiomorbidity analysis of 72 long-term conditions. For each condition, we maximised the available sample size for GWAS. Where possible, we preferentially used published meta-analysis consortium data. Where possible, we meta-analysed with UK Biobank and/or Finngen. If no appropriate published GWAS was available at the time of meta-analysis (May 2023) we used just UK Biobank, or UK Biobank meta-analysed with FinnGen (where comparable endpoint was available). Meta-analysis performed using GWAMA software.
For this long-term condition (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disorder [COPD]) Meta-analysis of UKB and FinnGen.
Effective N = 161709
Base-pair locations are for human genome build 37
